topic: Triangle similarity --- diagnosing reversed correspondence and scale-factor errors

traps.desc: reused the 9 cm side in place of the 8 cm side, solving 6/9 = 9/EF

problems.desc: Part (b) rubric: a correct response says the proportion put the 9 cm side in the numerator of the second ratio, where the 8 cm side of the first triangle belongs; the two ratios must compare matching sides of the two triangles, one side from each. Naming the mismatched pair is required for full credit.

traps.desc: turned the second ratio upside down, solving 10/4 = TU/15

problems.desc: Part (b) rubric: a correct response says the second ratio was written upside down --- the unknown side of the smaller triangle must sit in the same position (denominator) as the other side of that same triangle. A response that only recomputes the number without naming the inversion earns partial credit.

traps.desc: used the reciprocal scale factor and shrank the side instead of enlarging it

problems.desc: Part (c) rubric: a correct response says the scale factor was written the wrong way round --- going from the smaller triangle to the larger one the factor is the larger length over the smaller, so it must be greater than 1, and multiplying by a factor below 1 shrinks a side that should grow. Full credit needs the direction stated, not just the corrected arithmetic.

traps.desc: matched P with K instead of L and copied the 75 degree angle

problems.desc: Part (b) rubric: a correct response says the similarity statement pairs the third vertex of one triangle with the third vertex of the other, so P corresponds to L and not to K; the copied measure belongs to the second vertex pair. Full credit requires the correct pairing to be named.

traps.desc: multiplied the full-size side by 4 instead of dividing by it

problems.desc: Part (b) rubric: a correct response says a factor of 4 describes going from the model to the full-size object, so travelling the other way the side must be divided by 4 rather than multiplied; a model side longer than the object it copies is the signal that the direction was reversed. Full credit requires the direction to be stated in words.

traps.desc: wrote the second ratio upside down as 15/10

problems.desc: Part (b) rubric: a correct response says both ratios must be read in the same order --- first triangle over second triangle on each side of the equation --- and that the second ratio was written with the sides swapped, which inflates the value of the unknown. Full credit requires naming the swap, not just producing the right number.
